# 4. The study in one page

**Question.** When retail fuel prices rise, do poor Filipino households (bottom
30%) face larger price increases than all households, and does this differ by
region? Target journal: *Asian Economic Journal*. The design copies the local
projections of Kpodar and Liu (2022, *Energy Economics* 108:105909).

**Notation.** Here *t* is the month, *r* the region and *k* the spending
category. Group *A* is all income households and group *B* the bottom 30%.

- Fuel shock: $f_t = 100\,\Delta \ln F_t$, where $F$ is PSA CPI sub-index 07.2.2.
- Inflation: $\pi^g_t = 100\,\Delta\ln P^g_t$.
- Gap: $D_t = 100\ln(P^A_t/P^B_t)$, so $\Delta D_t = \pi^A_t-\pi^B_t$. A
  negative change in the gap means the shock is regressive.
- Pass-through: $\beta_h$. Cumulative pass-through: $B_h=\sum_{j\le h}\beta_j$.

**Model (one regression per horizon $h=0,\dots,12$).**
$$\pi_{t+h}=\alpha_h+\beta_h f_t+\sum_{q=1}^{12}\gamma_q\pi_{t-q}+\sum_{q=1}^{12}\lambda_q f_{t-q}+\sum_{l=1}^{h-1}\rho_l f_{t+l}+\delta_h t+\varepsilon_{t+h}$$

The terms are as follows:

- the third sum holds the Teulings–Zubanov leads;
- the data are not seasonally adjusted;
- national models use Newey–West standard errors with $h+1$ lags;
- the regional panel has region fixed effects and Driscoll–Kraay standard errors;
- bands are 90%.

The estimator is in `ospd/lp.py`.

**Theory used in the FA2 proposal.**

- Cost-push pricing, from the Leontief input–output price model (Miller & Blair, 2009): $\pi_k\approx\phi_k f$.
- Cost-of-living index: $\pi^g\approx\sum_k w^g_k\pi_k=\Phi^g f$.
- Gap decomposition into a weights effect and a within-category effect.
- Deaton (1989): the welfare cost of a price rise is the budget-share-weighted price change.
- Oil-specific theory:
  - Kilian (2008): direct and indirect channels;
  - Blanchard & Galí (2010): second-round effects;
  - Arze del Granado, Coady & Gillingham (2012): fuel price incidence.

# 5. Data facts (answers to questions the user asked)

**Regional monthly data.** All three main series are monthly, by region, and
come from PSA OpenSTAT:

| Series | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Retail fuel index 07.2.2 | 1994–Aug 2026, all 17 regions |
| All-income CPI | 1994–Aug 2026, all 17 regions |
| Bottom-30% CPI, all items | 2000–Aug 2026, all 17 regions |
| Bottom-30% CPI, by commodity | 2012–Aug 2026, all 17 regions |

All are on the 2018 = 100 basis, using PSA's own backcasts. Gasoline alone
(07.2.2.2) exists only from 2018. No official regional *peso-per-litre* pump
price series is available for this span. The World Bank series is Manila only,
2017–Apr 2025.

**Regions that change over time (decision D6).** PSA publishes two codings:

- the old 17-region code, in which Negros is split between Regions VI and VII;
- the new code, in which the Negros Island Region (NIR) is separate, following its 2024 re-creation.

The backcasts exist only on the old code, so the panel uses the old 17 regions
throughout. The two codings are identical for all other regions and nationally
over 2018–2025.

For Jan–Aug 2026, only new-code data exist. We chain the new-code monthly growth
onto the old-code levels and flag those months `new_geo_ext` for VI, VII, XII and
BARMM; robustness check (k) drops them.

BARMM: PSA publishes one unbroken series. Whether the pre-2019 values use the
ARMM or the BARMM boundary (Cotabato City) is still unconfirmed (open question).
Leave-one-region-out covers it.

**Who made the "all income" and "bottom 30%" categories?** PSA did. Both CPIs
are official PSA statistics:

- *CPI for All Income Households* is the headline CPI.
- *CPI for the Bottom 30% Income Households* uses the expenditure weights of
  households in the poorest 30% of the per-capita income distribution in the
  Family Income and Expenditure Survey.

Only the **inflation gap** $D$ is our construction: the log ratio of the two
official indices.

**Who made the region groups?** We did. They were pre-specified on 2026-10-04,
before any estimate (decision D8), from PSA data. The rules are listed below;
the group membership is in `output/tables/region_groups.csv`.

| Group | Rule | Regions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High poverty | 2018 poverty incidence above the 17-region median | V, VIII, IX, X, XI, XII, XIII, BARMM |
| High food share | Food weight in the region's 2018 all-income basket above the median | II, MIMAROPA, V, VIII, IX, XII, XIII, BARMM |
| Mindanao | Geography | IX, X, XI, XII, XIII, BARMM |
| Island regions | Geography | MIMAROPA, VI, VII, VIII |

These are analytical choices, not PSA categories, and the paper must say so.

**What proxies the oil shock?** The main shock in every model, 2001–2026
including 2026, is the monthly log change of **PSA CPI 07.2.2, "Fuels and
lubricants for personal transport"**, national and by region (decision D5).

Over 2016–2025 its monthly changes correlate 0.87 with the World Bank Manila
RON91 pump price and 0.99 with 07.2.2.2 gasoline.

Robustness shocks:

- **Dubai crude in pesos:** World Bank Pink Sheet × BSP peso–dollar rate.
- **Gasoline 07.2.2.2:** from 2019.
- **World Bank Manila pump price:** 2018–Mar 2025.
- **National instead of regional 07.2.2:** in the panel.

For the 2026 episode (E1–E3), the models are estimated to Dec 2025. They are then
fed the actual Jan–Aug 2026 path of 07.2.2, national or regional.

The EU validation uses the Weekly Oil Bulletin pump prices, before and after tax,
and Brent in euro.

# 6. Results so far (all in `output/tables/`; numbers are generated, not typed)

**RQ1.** Cumulative pass-through to the all-income CPI is 0.044 on impact, 0.087
at 6 months and 0.102 at 12 months. The bottom-30% CPI is similar. With crude oil
as the shock it is about 40% as large.

**RQ2.** The national gap is regressive:

- −0.0155 at $h=6$, −0.0097 at $h=12$; significant only at some horizons.
- The regional panel gives −0.021 at $h=6$ and −0.017 at $h=12$, both significant.
- The effect is weaker after 2013.
- It is about zero with macro controls, with the gasoline index, and with the World Bank pump price.

**RQ3.** Pass-through is largest in transport (0.37), housing and utilities
(0.16) and food (0.07). The weights alone predict a *progressive* gap (+0.010),
so the regressive result comes from within-category price differences.

**RQ4.** The interaction for Mindanao is −0.017, for island regions −0.012 and
for high poverty −0.010. None survives a Bonferroni correction.

**2026 episode.** A model estimated to Dec 2025 explains about half of the actual
Dec 2025–Aug 2026 rise: 2.55 of 4.81 log points (all income) and 3.13 of 5.98
(bottom 30%). The fuel-driven cost to a poverty-line family of five is PHP
467/month nationally, PHP 390–633 by region. Cereals explain most of the 2026
gap.

**Replication gate.** It passed:

| Shock | Ours | Paper |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After tax | 0.057 | 0.055 |
| Before tax | 0.024 | 0.020 |
| Brent | 0.014 | 0.015 |
